paragraphs.text: وَإِن طَآئِفَتَانِ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ٱقْتَتَلُوا۟ فَأَصْلِحُوا۟ بَيْنَهُمَا ۖ فَإِنۢ بَغَتْ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا عَلَى ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ فَقَـٰتِلُوا۟ ٱلَّتِى تَبْغِى حَتَّىٰ تَفِىٓءَ إِلَىٰٓ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ فَإِن فَآءَتْ فَأَصْلِحُوا۟ بَيْنَهُمَا بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَأَقْسِطُوٓا۟ ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُقْسِطِينَ

en.text: Category / theme: Qur’anic evidence • Peace Maker

Published English translation: And if two parties of believers fall to fighting, then make peace between them. And if one party of them doeth wrong to the other, fight ye that which doeth wrong till it return unto the ordinance of Allah; then, if it return, make peace between them justly, and act equitably. Lo! Allah loveth the equitable.
Source: Al-Hujurat (49:9)
Translation: Marmaduke Pickthall — Tanzil text, en.pickthall
Status: Arabic and the identified published translation checked.
Relevance (compiler): Addresses conflict between believers and conditions settlement on justice; it is not an unqualified endorsement of passivity or a verbatim modern international-law rule.
Best use: Principle / argument
Related references: 150
Verify:
Arabic
Pickthall
Jalandhry
